content: I'll start by reading the test image and the part index file simultaneously.

The test image shows a **stem at soil level** with whitish/grayish mycelial growth and possible sclerotia at the crown area. This is clearly a stem disease. Key features:
- White/grayish bleached tissue at the stem base
- Appears to be white mycelial coating on the stem
- Dark round bodies visible (possible sclerotia)
- Healthy green upper stem transitioning to diseased area at soil line

From the part index, stem diseases include: Southern_Blight, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Phytophthora_Blight, Rhizopus_Soft_Rots, Gray_Mold, Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, etc.

Top candidates based on visual: Southern_Blight (white mycelium + sclerotia at soil line) and Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot. Let me view reference images one at a time.
Southern Blight shows dense white mycelial growth at the soil line with sclerotia, which closely matches the test image. Now let me check Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.
Sclerotinia shows larger, more irregular black sclerotia and bleached stems. Now let me view two more candidates to cover the required 4 classes.
Phytophthora Blight shows dark brown/black lesions on fruit and stems - doesn't match the white mycelium pattern. Now the 4th class:

Rhizopus Soft Rots shows soft, mushy fruit rot with grayish-brown mycelium - clearly doesn't match the test image.

**Analysis summary:**

- **Test image**: Tomato stem at soil level with **dense white/grayish mycelial coating** and **small dark round structures** (sclerotia) on the bleached stem crown area. Black plastic mulch visible in background.

- **Southern_Blight** matches best: white cottony mycelium at soil line, small round sclerotia (mustard-seed sized turning tan/brown), stem rot at crown. The reference images even show the identical context (plants growing through black plastic mulch with white mycelium at the base).

- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** is similar but its sclerotia are larger, more irregular (rat-dropping shaped), and it typically affects the upper stem rather than the soil-line crown.

- **Phytophthora_Blight**: dark brown lesions on fruit/stems - ruled out.

- **Rhizopus_Soft_Rots**: brown soft rot on fruit with gray-brown fuzzy mycelium - ruled out.
